item.title: Finance Manager at SevenTwenty Holdings Ltd
item.description:
Seven Twenty Holdings Ltd is a company based in Kenya. The company specializes in the manufacturing of curtain rods and curtain rods accessories. It also manufactures paint. It has two main brands Executive Curtain Rods and Set Paints.Role Purpose
To provide strategic financial leadership at Seven Twenty Holdings, overseeing all financial management,reporting, controls, and compliance.
The Head of Finance will be responsible for building a robust financial controls environment, driving the integrity of ERP-integrated financial data, and providing management with the financial insight required to make informed business decisions in a manufacturing and distribution context.
Key Responsibilities
Financial Leadership & Strategy
Provide strategic financial direction and analysis to the Managing Director and senior management team
Lead the preparation of monthly, quarterly, and annual management accounts
Develop and monitor annual budgets, forecasts, and cash flow projections
Provide commercial analysis including product margin analysis, cost of production reporting and pricing support
Present financial results and commentary to management and the Board
Financial Controls & Compliance
Design, implement, and maintain a comprehensive internal controls framework
Establish and enforce month-end close procedures including account sign-off and period locking in Odoo
Review and approve all manual journal entries, prior period adjustments, and balance sheet reclassifications
Ensure all statutory requirements are met including VAT, corporate tax, and financial reporting obligations
Manage the external audit process and be the primary point of contact for auditors
ERP & Systems Oversight (Odoo)
Take ownership of the Odoo accounting configuration including chart of accounts, product category account mappings, and journal settings
Review and approve all system configuration changes that affect financial postings
Oversee the resolution of all historical posting errors and ensure correcting journals are accurate, authorised, and documented
Drive monthly reconciliation of inventory valuation reports to the general ledger
Ensure work order templates, BOMs, and manufacturing configurations are correctly set up before use
Inventory & Manufacturing Finance
Oversee the financial management of all inventory including raw materials, WIP, and finished goods
Ensure monthly reconciliation of Stock Interim Delivered, Stock Interim Received, and WIP accounts
Review the weekly production WIP report prepared by the Production Manager and reconcile to Odoo
Ensure all Bills of Materials are costed accurately and updated whenever input costs change
Monitor and investigate all stock variances, ensuring appropriate authorisation and accounting treatment
Team Management & Development
Lead, supervise, and develop the finance team, setting clear objectives and performance standards
 Identify skills gaps within the finance team and implement training and upskilling plans
 Ensure clear segregation of duties within the finance function
 Build a finance team culture of accuracy, accountability, and continuous improvemen
Qualifications & Experience
Requirement Details
Education CPA(K) or ACCA qualified. Bachelor\'s degree in Finance, Accounting, or Commerce
Experience Minimum 5 years in finance, with at least 2 years in a senior finance management role 
Industry Manufacturing, FMCG, or industrial operations experience strongly preferred
ERP Systems Hands-on experience with Odoo, SAP, Sage, or equivalent ERP. Odoo preferred
Technical Skills
Advanced Excel, financial modelling, cost accounting, inventory finance,and management reporting.
Personal Attributes 
Strong leadership, high integrity, analytical mindset, and the ability to work in a fast-paced operational environment.
What we offer:
Compensation of KES. 100,000 [net] per month amongst other mandatory statutory benefits
A conducive environment with strong orientation to the organization and continuous  support.

item.title: Underwriting Assistant at Geminia Life Insurance
item.description:
Geminia Life Insurance Company Limited is a Kenyan-owned insurance company which specializes in Life Insurance. The company was established after Geminia Insurance Company Limited separated its General and Life insurance business.
Geminia Life Insurance Company has a proven track record of rendering efficient and personalized life insurance solutions to all its clients since 1982 and providing well thought-out Insurance, investment, and retirement solutionsJOB SUMMARY: 
To support the underwriting of individual and group life insurance businesses by assessing risks, processing new business and renewals, and providing accurate and timely policy servicing in line with company underwriting guidelines, delegated authority, risk appetite, and regulatory requirements.
 KEY RESPONSIBILITIES: 
Review and assess individual and group life insurance proposals and supporting documentation.
Conduct basic medical and financial risk assessment in accordance with underwriting guidelines.
Process new business, renewals, alterations, endorsements, reinstatements, and other policy transactions.
Assist in underwriting corporate/group life schemes, including preparation of quotations and renewal terms.
Review medical reports, claims experience, member schedules, and other relevant risk information.
Ensure accurate application of terms, exclusions, loadings, benefits, and sums assured.
Identify and refer risks outside delegated authority or the company’s risk appetite.
Maintain accurate underwriting and policy records in the system.
Follow up on outstanding medical, financial, and other underwriting requirements.
Liaise with intermediaries, corporate clients, and internal departments on underwriting and servicing matters.
Ensure compliance with company policies, regulatory requirements, and underwriting procedures.
Maintain confidentiality of customer, medical, and financial information.
Prepare routine underwriting reports and perform other duties assigned by an authorized officer.
Key Performance Indicators: 
Risk assessment and analytical skills.
Attention to detail and accuracy.
Good numerical and communication skills.
Customer and intermediary service orientation.
Good organizational and time management skills.
Integrity and ability to maintain confidentiality.
Good knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word.
Ability to work within deadlines and delegated authority.
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in insurance, Actuarial Science, Risk Management, Finance, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field.
Progress towards professional insurance qualification AIIK/CII/ACII/COP is an added advantage.
Experience
1-year relevant experience in life insurance, preferably in underwriting or insurance operations.
Exposure to individual and group/corporate life underwriting is desirable.
Experience using the TurnQuest System is preferred.

item.title: Senior Legal Counsel- Litigation at KCB Bank Kenya
item.description:
Kenya Commercial Bank Limited is registered as a non-operating holding company which started operations as a licensed banking institution with effect from January 1, 2016. The holding company oversees KCB Kenya - incorporated with effect from January 1, 2016 - and all KCB's regional units in Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Burundi, Ethiopia and South Sudan. It also owns KCB Insurance Agency, KCB Capital, KCB Foundation and all associate companies. The holding company was set up to among other things to enhance the Group's capacity to access unrestricted capital and also enable investment in new ventures outside banking regulations, achieve operational and strategic autonomy for the Group's operating entities and enhance corporate governance across the Group and oversight in management of subsidiaries.KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
For the assigned portfolio of work, conduct legal research, collate evidence, prepare witnesses for pre-trial and hearing, develop concept papers, prepare legal briefs and opinions as well as develop effective defense strategies, arguments and testimony in preparation for legal proceedings of cases in liaison with external lawyers.
Represent the Bank before any court or tribunal as a witness or to watch brief as necessary.
Manage and measure external lawyers’ performance to ensure efficiency.
Create legal awareness and provide advice on suitable action to avert and/or minimize litigation.
Scrutinize legal fees and ensure they are raised in accordance with the Remuneration Order and Service Level Agreement.
Update database of all non-debt recovery litigation to ensure the same is consistently up-to-date and provide reports as may be required.
Render legal guidance to Retail branches on matters relating to bank policies, processes and procedures on all queries received with a view to mitigating legal and reputational risks.
For the above position, the ideal candidate should possess the following qualifications and experience:
A bachelor’s degree in law.
A Diploma in Law.
At least 5 years of legal experience.
A minimum of 4 years of experience in legal drafting.
4 years of experience in Corporate Governance.
4 years of experience in Risk Management.
3 years of experience in legal communication and advocacy.

item.title: Global Foundations Manager at Welthungerhilfe
item.description:
Welthungerhilfe is one of the largest Non-Governmental aid agencies in Germany providing long term development assistance projects.
Welthungerhilfe has supported Kenyan development organizations since its establishment in 1962. It has had an office in Nairobi since its registration as an NGO operating in Kenya since 1993. Geographically, Welthungerhilfe's intervention areas in Kenya have mainly been in the arid and semi-arid zones of Kajiado, Makueni, Kitui, Tana River, Marsabit and Garissa Counties. Most recently in 2012, Welthungerhilfe started implementing interventions in Nairobi County and in 2015 expanded to Kakamega, Vihiga and Siaya Counties as well as Turkana, Wajir and Mandera Counties working with partners. The Kenya Country Programme is also responsible for Welthungerhilfeâs operations in Somalia and Tanzania.Your responsibilities
Work closely with country offices to identify, develop, and advance strategic foundation partnership opportunities.
Collaborate with country teams in building and managing strong foundation prospect pipelines, identifying opportunities that align with programmatic priorities and funding strategies.
Accompany country offices in the cultivation and development of foundation partnerships, including donor outreach strategies, engagement planning, and partnership positioning.
Contribute to developing partnership pitches, concepts, and cases for support together with country teams, translating programmatic priorities and impact evidence into compelling foundation-facing propositions.
Facilitate exchange of successful practices, market insights, and fundraising approaches across country offices to strengthen the organization’s overall capacity to engage foundations.
Identify and pursue selected strategic foundation opportunities, particularly with regional or locally present foundations, in close coordination with relevant country offices and head office colleagues.
Coordinate closely with WHH colleagues wordwide to ensure aligned relationship management and coordinated donor engagement.
Develop high-quality pitches, concept notes, proposals, and partnership propositions in collaboration with technical experts, program and country teams.
Support due diligence processes and risk assessments for prospective foundation partners in line with Welthungerhilfe’s policies and compliance requirements.
Your profile
A Bachelor’s degree required; a Master’s degree in a relevant field (e.g. International Relations, Nonprofit Management, Development Studies, Marketing, or Communications) is strongly preferred. 
At least five years of progressive experience in foundation fundraising or institutional philanthropy, ideally within an international NGO or global development context.
Demonstrated ability to secure six- and seven-figure grants from foundations and manage long-term donor relationships.
Strong analytical and strategic skills to translate complex programmatic information into compelling, impact-driven funding propositions.
Experience using donor relationship management systems (e.g., Salesforce or equivalent) to maintain a structured partner pipeline and monitor engagement.
Excellent interpersonal and networking skills with the ability to build trust and collaborate effectively across cultures, functions, and levels of seniority.
High degree of independence, organization, and reliability, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results in a dynamic environment.
Ability to thrive in a dynamic, fast-paced environment and adapt strategies to evolving philanthropic trends.
You recognize the growing value of data in your field and are eager to build your awareness and skills to incorporate data-informed approaches into your work.
Exceptional written and verbal English skills, with proven ability to develop persuasive, donor-oriented proposals and reports. Proficiency in additional languages is an asset.
What we offer
Fair Compensation: A fair and equal remuneration based on a transparent salary scale.
Commitment to Well-Being: We attach great importance to our duty of care with a focus on safety, security & health.
Modern & Agile Work Environment: Be part of a forward thinking organization that fully embraces digitalization and innovation across all areas.
Personal & Professional Growth: Access diverse learning and development opportunities to advance your career.
Team: Join our dedicated and diverse teams, where passion, expertise, and joy come together to create a better world.

item.title: Chief Program Officer at Living Goods
item.description:
At Living Goods we empower people to improve the health of their families, friends and communities. Living Goods supports networks of 'Avon-likeâ health entrepreneurs who go door to door to teach families how to improve their health and wealth and sell life-changing products such as simple treatments for malaria and diarrhea, safe delivery kits, fortified foods, clean cook stoves, water filters, and solar lights. By combining the best practices from business and public health, we are dramatically lowering child mortality AND creating livelihoods for thousands of enterprising women.
Living Goods supports a network of over 2,000 micro-entrepreneurs in Uganda and Kenya who teach families in their communities how to improve health and well-being while selling affordable, high-impact products like basic medicines, fortified foods, water filters, clean cook-stoves, and solar lights. As part of the Branch Team, you will play a key role in supporting Community Health Volunteers (CHVs) to deliver high quality health care to their communities and generate sales of critical products.About the Role
Living Goods is hiring a Chief Program Officer to lead programs that bring life-saving health services to millions of families.
The Chief Program Officer (CPO) provides strategic leadership and operational oversight across Living Goods' global program portfolio, ensuring high-quality, evidence-driven delivery at scale. The CPO sets program strategy and priorities, stewards the frameworks and tools that enable consistent country-level execution, and leads the organization's Performance, Evidence and Insights function, ensuring that robust evidence, learning, and performance insights drive strategic decision-making, program improvement, and organizational impact.
The role also shapes Living Goods' innovation agenda, stewarding the pipeline of new approaches, tools, and delivery models from concept through adoption and scale to define the next frontier of community health impact. Critically, the CPO serves as the connective tissue between program and technology, ensuring that digital health tools and data systems are purposefully embedded into delivery models to strengthen community health worker performance and improve health outcomes.
The CPO leads disciplined geographic expansion, strengthens donor and fundraising alignment, and ensures that program knowledge is systematically generated, captured, and shared across the organization, maximizing Living Goods' impact, efficiency, and scale
Reporting Scope
The Chief Program Officer (CPO) reports to the Chief Executive Officer and serves as a member of the Global Executive Team. The role provides strategic leadership and oversight across the organization's Performance, Evidence and Insights, Innovation, Program Strategy, and Country Incubation functions, with accountability for program strategy, budget stewardship, fund transfers, and decision-making as set out in Living Goods' Delegation of Authority Framework.
Key Responsibilities
Program Strategy & Portfolio Support: (30% of time)
Provide strategic direction and shared capabilities that countries can draw on to strengthen impact, efficiency, and scale. 
Set global program strategy and priorities across existing and new initiatives, aligned with Living Goods' strategy and Theory of Change. 
Enable strategic portfolio prioritization and trade-offs, offering frameworks and insights to inform leadership decision-making. 
Shape geographic expansion and portfolio evolution, including criteria for scale, focus, consolidation, or exit. 
Set strategic direction for the innovation pipeline and its pathways to country adoption and scale. 
Build and steward strategic partnerships, including new government partnerships that countries can leverage where they add value. 
Shape fundraising priorities and decisions based on program strategy and performance insights.
Execution for Impact: (20% of time)
Strengthen country-level delivery performance by providing shared frameworks, digital and data tools, and performance oversight — ensuring technology serves as a force multiplier for program quality and efficacy.
Design and steward global program frameworks, standards, and models based on evidence to guide consistent, high-quality delivery at country level.
Own and evolve the performance operating system — including tools, practices, and ROI focus — used across countries.
Enable cross-country performance review, learning, and continuous improvement.
Drive and monitor the innovation stage gates to optimize innovation pipeline delivery and lifecycle.
Serve as the programmatic voice in shaping how digital health tools are designed and deployed — partnering closely with the CTO to ensure technology investments are grounded in frontline delivery realities and community health worker needs, rather than owning the technology itself.
Work with the technology team to ensure shared digital and data tools are fit-for-purpose, translating program requirements into actionable inputs for the technology roadmap.
Ensure that digital tools genuinely support community health worker performance and that adoption is embedded in program quality standards.
Improve ways of working, systems, and processes between global and country teams to reduce friction and duplication..
Performance, Evidence and Insights: (20 % of time)
Generate decision-grade evidence and insights to inform strategy, strengthen programs, and improve outcomes.
Ensure robust analytics, monitoring, and independent research and evaluations across programs and innovations to build credible evidence and learning.
Generate and synthesize insights from data and evidence to inform program design, performance, and decision-making.
Translate evidence into clear insights and narratives for countries, leadership, partners, and donors.
Ensure the documentation and knowledge management system is effective in supporting learning, replication, scale, and the organization's thought leadership agenda.
New Countries: (15% of time)
Enable disciplined, repeatable expansion through a clear country scoping and incubation model.
Define and apply criteria for scoping new countries, aligned to strategy and organizational capacity.
Design and steward the new country incubation model, including time-bound global support.
Support and oversee countries during incubation, including direct accountability for readiness and transition to a core country.
Fundraising and Donor Delivery: (15% of time)
Ensure programmatic integrity and alignment from proposal through delivery and reporting.
Ensure funding proposals are programmatically sound.
Provide programmatic input to donor engagement where technical credibility is required.
Oversee delivery against grant commitments and surface risks early.
Ensure accurate and coherent programmatic reporting.
Leadership: (Across)
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing global programs team, fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, and continuous learning.
Serve as a key member of the Senior Leadership Team, contributing to organizational strategy, culture, and cross-functional decision-making.
Model Living Goods' values and champion equity, inclusion, and community-centred program design.
Represent Living Goods externally with donors, partners, governments, and global health stakeholders.
The Person We Are Looking For
Living Goods is looking for a strategic program leader who has driven multi-country health delivery at scale and who works fluently across program and technology.
This is a role defined by strategic leadership, evidence rigor, and the ability to translate program needs into technology priorities without owning technology delivery itself.
What the Role Requires
Master's degree or equivalent in public health, international development, business administration, or a related discipline preferred; bachelor's degree required.
15+ years of progressive leadership experience in global health, international development, or a related field, with significant time working in sub-Saharan Africa.
Proven track record leading large-scale, multi-country program delivery — ideally in primary healthcare or last-mile service delivery.
Demonstrated ability to work at the intersection of program and technology, translating digital health investments into measurable impact.
Experience managing and developing senior teams across geographies and cultures.
Track record of successful donor engagement, fundraising, and grant management.
Private sector experience is a serious advantage.
Bilingual French and English is a serious advantage.
Willing to travel 30%+ of the time.
Role based in Nairobi.
